name: rscrypto
baseline: ring 0.17.14 and aws-lc-rs 1.18.1 (AWS-LC-backed AEAD), plus RustCrypto aes-gcm/chacha20poly1305 crates
workload: Criterion-benchmarked AES-128/256-GCM, AES-128/256-GCM-SIV, ChaCha20-Poly1305 and XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD seal/open at multiple buffer sizes, run on 8 Linux CPU platforms (AMD Zen4/Zen5, AWS Graviton3/4, IBM Power10, IBM z16/s390x, Intel Ice Lake, Intel Sapphire Rapids) with each case matched against the fastest external crate for that case
claimed_speedup: aes-128-gcm 1.80x fastest-external geomean (2.01x across all matched crates); aes-256-gcm 1.83x (2.02x all); aes-128-gcm-siv 2.20x (2.92x all); aes-256-gcm-siv 2.34x (3.16x all); chacha20-poly1305 1.12x fastest-external (1.32x all); xchacha20-poly1305 1.43x. AEAD-wide: 1.61x geomean across 1,408 fastest-external Criterion rows, W/T/L 910/288/210
compiler_and_flags: rustc 1.98.1 for native x86_64/aarch64 CI jobs, 1.99.0-nightly (3d6c19bb9) for cross-built POWER/s390x/RISC-V; `cargo bench` release profile; RUSTFLAGS/target-cpu policy per docs/benchmarking.md (explicit RUSTFLAGS honored, else -C target-cpu=native)
hardware: GitHub Actions run #34874736834 on AWS EC2 c8a.2xlarge (AMD), c8i.2xlarge (Intel), c9g.2xlarge (Graviton, aarch64), plus native POWER/s390x/RISC-V runners; separate 8-host Linux headline matrix: AMD Zen4, AMD Zen5, AWS Graviton3, AWS Graviton4, IBM Power10, IBM z16/s390x, Intel Ice Lake, Intel Sapphire Rapids
tradeoffs: Pure-Rust with target-gated SIMD/assembly kernels, no OpenSSL/libsodium FFI dependency, no_std/WASM support; project self-reports several loss areas (e.g. ECDSA P-384 sign 0.70x vs aws-lc-rs) and has not funded a third-party security audit
caveats: Headline ratios are geomeans over many buffer-size/platform pairs rather than one reproducible number; the project's own docs repeatedly withdraw or re-caveat older aggregates ('workload identity' and 'comparison validity' corrections), so treat this as a vendor-run but methodologically transparent CI benchmark, not independent third-party verification; none of the compared crates is literally OpenSSL or libsodium, so baseline_in_list is false even though ring/aws-lc-rs are widely used native-speed incumbents
found_via: HN Algolia query 'Ascon AEAD faster' surfaced Show HN: Rscrypto, pure-Rust crypto with industry leading public benches -> https://github.com/loadingalias/rscrypto

name: Cloudflare ChaCha20-Poly1305 OpenSSL patch (sslconfig)
workload: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD 'seal' operation with 13 bytes of AAD (TLS-record-shaped), plaintext sizes from 64 bytes to 16 KB, on a Haswell-generation CPU
claimed_speedup: Cloudflare's patched ChaCha20-Poly1305 significantly outperforms OpenSSL 1.1.0-pre for short records and is slightly faster for long records, average advantage ~7%; the post also notes AES-128/256-GCM (with AES-NI) still beat ChaCha20-Poly1305 for records over 320 bytes, reaching below 2 cycles/byte
hardware: Haswell-generation CPU (exact model not stated); post notes Broadwell/Skylake give AES-GCM a further edge
tradeoffs: Patch targets OpenSSL's cipher-suite ordering/implementation for TLS ChaCha20-Poly1305, supporting both the pre-RFC draft and RFC 7905 cipher-suite IDs
caveats: Numbers are read off graphs in the post, not a data table; no compiler flags stated; the post dates to April 2016 and benchmarks an OpenSSL 1.1.0 pre-release, so absolute figures are stale even though the qualitative result (near-parity/slight win over stock OpenSSL ChaCha20-Poly1305 for short records) is historically well known. repo_url is on the KNOWN_LIST (already catalogued), reported here only as evidence for that known entry per is_evidence_for_known.
found_via: WebFetch of https://blog.cloudflare.com/it-takes-two-to-chacha-poly/, reached via HN Algolia search 'AES-NI vs ChaCha20' comment thread
